changed.title: Cyclic binary window tables simulate permutation programs with a unique indexed word on acceptance
changed.statement:
∀ (d m t : ℕ),
  let w := d + 1
  let State := Fin w → Bool
  let blockLen := w * (2 * d + 1)
  let n := t * blockLen + w
  let hb : 0 < blockLen := by dsimp [blockLen, w]; positivity
  let hn : 0 < n := by dsimp [n, w]; positivity
  ∀ (query : Fin t → Fin m) (step : Fin t → Bool → Equiv.Perm State)
    (start finish : State),
    let Pattern := Fin (w + 1) → Bool
    ∃ (block : Fin t → Bool → Fin blockLen → Pattern → Bool)
      (pin : Fin w → Pattern → Bool),
      ∀ x : Fin m → Bool,
        let row := fun (i : Fin n) =>
          if h : i.val / blockLen < t then
            let instr : Fin t := ⟨i.val / blockLen, h⟩
            block instr (x (query instr)) ⟨i.val % blockLen, Nat.mod_lt _ hb⟩
          else
            pin (Fin.ofNat (d + 1) (i.val - t * blockLen))
        let ok := fun (word : Fin n → Bool) => ∀ j : Fin n,
          row j (fun k => word ⟨(j.val + k.val) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩) = true
        let lastState := (List.finRange t).foldl (fun a s => step s (x (query s)) a) start
        (Finset.univ.filter ok).card = if lastState = finish then 1 else 0
changed.unlocks: encodes permutation branching programs by cyclic tests while preserving the number of accepting words
changed.context: Route each chosen permutation through 2w-1 layers of switches on coordinate pairs. For the induction, pair inputs and outputs on coordinate zero. Permutation edges form a degree-two bipartite multigraph on pairs. Color cycles alternately, sending one of each color through each pair. Recurse inside each color. Each switch layer takes w shifts: copy each dropped bit except on the chosen coordinate, where the other bits determine whether to flip. In the final w shifts require the dropped target bits and append start bits. Closure then selects one run.

changed.title: At most 2+e private rows have distinct profiles outside a narrow column set in an AND/OR region with e at most one entry wire
changed.statement:
∀ (n m d : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
    (R : Finset (Fin n)) (B : Finset (Fin m)) (region entry : Finset ℕ) (top : ℕ),
  let raw := n + m
  let sources := R.image (fun sourceRow => sourceRow.val) ∪ B.image (fun sourceCol => n + sourceCol.val)
  let inside := fun (w : ℕ) => raw ≤ w ∧ w - raw ∈ region
  let gate := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C
  (∀ firstRow secondRow : Fin n, firstRow ≠ secondRow → d ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun col => G firstRow col ≠ G secondRow col)).card) →
  (∀ firstCol secondCol : Fin m, firstCol ≠ secondCol → d ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun row => G row firstCol ≠ G row secondCol)).card) →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack raw C →
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C → region ⊆ Finset.range C.size → top ∈ region →
  entry.card ≤ 1 → (∀ w ∈ entry, w < raw + top ∧ w ∉ sources ∧ ¬ inside w) →
  (∀ k ∈ region,
    ((gate k).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∨
     (gate k).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or) ∧
    ∀ w ∈ (gate k).inputs, w ∈ sources ∨ inside w ∨ w ∈ entry) →
  (∀ k < C.size, k ∉ region → ∀ w ∈ (gate k).inputs,
    w ∉ sources ∧ (inside w → w = raw + top)) →
  C.output ∉ sources → (inside C.output → C.output = raw + top) →
  (B.card < d → R.card ≤ 2 + entry.card) ∧ (R.card < d → B.card ≤ 2 + entry.card)
changed.unlocks: bounds the number of private rows or columns whose profiles differ outside a small opposite set
changed.context: Fix an active outside column and vary the active private row. Until the top, outside gates cannot read a private signal, so the entry value depends only on the column. In the region each row induces a monotone unary truth table on that bit, either zero, identity or one. Without an entry there are two constant tables. Equal tables give identical outputs on every outside column, since only the top leaves the region. Fewer than d private columns cannot hide d disagreements. Count the types and exchange sides. Gate-price companions cannot exist for a bound on private inputs.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 6 bipartite graph with mask 275444 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 11 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 4) (v : Fin 6) => (275444 : ℕ).testBit (6 * u.val + v.val)) 11
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 4 by 6 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 12 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out, equal gates merged and unread gates dropped); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 11; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 9 (on paper), a gap of 3. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 3 left, 4 to 9 right, gate j writes wire 10 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 24 inputs with one vertex on each side.

changed.title: The six-vertex edge function with table 18446461426206309032 has an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in at most two of at most VALUE gates, all counted, and none smaller
changed.template:
PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.HasCircuitSize 6 (fun x : Fin 6 → Bool => (18446461426206309032 : ℕ).testBit (PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.tableIndex x)) @@VALUE@@ ∧
  ∀ t : ℕ, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.HasCircuitSize 6 (fun x : Fin 6 → Bool => (18446461426206309032 : ℕ).testBit (PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.tableIndex x)) t → @@VALUE@@ ≤ t
changed.value_max_why: a 11-gate circuit, replayed on all 64 inputs by the hub (bound from a circuit replayed by the hub, not a checked row)
changed.size_in_words: AND, OR and NOT gates, each reading at most two wires, every gate counted including NOT gates
changed.unlocks: one exact entry of Table 2, the edge-function sizes with NOT gates (library data)
changed.sketch: A circuit of 11 gates for f is known (the hub replays it when posting), so the value is at most 11; that is an upper bound only, the value may be smaller. No NOT saving on a graph is on our tables. Give a circuit for the upper half and an LRAT refutation one gate below for the lower half, through PEqualNP.Library.LRAT.LinkN2 (NOT gates counted). Library data.
